description: Very slow ramps, triggers and gates following the computer's clock, from the current second through to the current year

params.text: Alt mode: reads the clock in UTC rather than in local time

outputs.text: A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current second
The second's ramp rounded down to 4 steps of 2.5V
10V through the first hundredth of each second and 0V for the rest of it, which is 10ms rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each second and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each second and 10V through the second half
A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current minute
The minute's ramp rounded down to 60 steps, one per second
10V through the first hundredth of each minute and 0V for the rest of it, which is 600ms rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each minute and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each minute and 10V through the second half
A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current hour
The hour's ramp rounded down to 24 steps of 2.5 minutes each, not the 60 one-minute steps the manual gives
10V through the first hundredth of each hour and 0V for the rest of it, which is 36 seconds rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each hour and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each hour and 10V through the second half
A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current day, starting at local midnight
The day's ramp rounded down to 7 steps of 3 hours 26 minutes each, not the 24 hourly steps the manual gives
10V through the first hundredth of each day and 0V for the rest of it, which is about 14 minutes rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each day and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each day and 10V through the second half
A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current week, starting at midnight on Sunday
The week's ramp rounded down to 4 steps of 1 day 18 hours each, not the 7 daily steps the manual gives
10V through the first hundredth of each week and 0V for the rest of it, which is about 100 minutes rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each week and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each week and 10V through the second half
A ramp rising from 0V to 10V across the current calendar month, the length of that month taken into account
The month's ramp rounded down to 12 steps, not the 4 weekly steps the manual gives
10V through the first hundredth of each month and 0V for the rest of it, which is about 7 hours rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each month and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each month and 10V through the second half
A ramp across the current three-month season, counted from January, that reaches 10V after 90 days
The season's ramp rounded down to 3 steps, one per month
10V through the first hundredth of each season and 0V for the rest of it, which is about 22 hours rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each season and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each season and 10V through the second half
A ramp across the current year that reaches 10V after 365 days, counted from local midnight on the 1st of January
The year's ramp rounded down to 12 steps of about 30 days each
10V through the first hundredth of each year and 0V for the rest of it, which is about 3 and a half days rather than the 1ms the manual gives
10V through the first half of each year and 0V through the second half
0V through the first half of each year and 10V through the second half

notes: nothing is patched into this module; every output follows the computer's own clock, in local time until the alt mode switch is flipped.
